claim: Bajaj's Chetak electric scooters are built in Pune (Chetak Technology plant at Akurdi)
source_quote: Chetak Technology Ltd today inaugurated their newly built EV manufacturing plant at Pune’s Akurdi on the birth anniversary of late Shri Rahul Bajaj.
note: Bajaj Auto press release, 10 Jun 2022 (primary). Cartoq (Aug 2025): Chetak lines at the Akurdi plant restarted on 20 Aug 2025. On-screen: PUNE · JULY 2025.

claim: Chetak production in July 2024 was 20,384 units (VO: about twenty thousand in a month)
source_quote: Bajaj Auto saw production of its Chetak electric scooter slump by 47 percent year-on-year (YoY) in July 2025, with just 10,824 units manufactured versus 20,384 units in July last year.
note: Second independent report: EVIndia (14 Aug 2025) gives the same 20,384 (Jul 2024) and 10,824 (Jul 2025). On-screen: 20,384 → 10,824 (−47%).

claim: Chetak production in July 2025 was 10,824 units (VO: less than eleven thousand)
source_quote: Bajaj Auto saw production of its Chetak electric scooter slump by 47 percent year-on-year (YoY) in July 2025, with just 10,824 units manufactured versus 20,384 units in July last year.
note: Same as R02; EVIndia 14 Aug 2025 agrees.

claim: The July 2025 Chetak drop was caused by a shortage of heavy rare earth magnets from China (not a strike or battery problem)
source_quote: The steep drop is a direct fallout of the ongoing shortage of heavy rare-earth magnets sourced from China.
note: Rajiv Bajaj to ET (Jul 2025) also blamed the unavailability of heavy rare earth magnets. 'No strike. No battery problem' is narration framing consistent with this.

claim: Most of the rare earth magnets India uses come from China (replacement wording for L3)
source_quote: with imports mainly from China, meeting most of the demand (nearly 60–80% by value and 85–90% by quantity between 2022–25)
note: REPLACES L3 '...and almost every one of them comes from China' (too strong: official share is 85-90% by quantity, about 85% by value per ICRA Jun 2025) with '...and most of them come from China.' Keeps L3 consistent with the new L15.

claim: The raw material (monazite) sits in beach sands in states including Andhra Pradesh, Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Odisha
source_quote: occurring in the coastal beach, teri / red sand and inland alluvium in parts of Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, Tamil Nadu, Kerala, West Bengal, Jharkhand, Gujarat and Maharashtra.
note: PIB (DAE, Parliament reply, 23 Jul 2025). IREL mines at Chavara (Kerala), Manavalakurichi (Tamil Nadu) and Chatrapur (Odisha) per ORF/IBM. Live vo.txt now names Andhra Pradesh too, which AMD lists first.

claim: By the Indian government's count, India's sands hold about seven million tonnes (7.23 Mt) of rare earth oxide (replacement for L5)
source_quote: Approximately 7.23 million tonne (Mt) in-situ Total Rare Earth Oxide Equivalent (TREO Eq.) contained in 13.15 Mt monazite [a mineral of thorium and Rare Earths] occurring in teri, beach sands and inland alluvium in parts of Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, Tamil Nadu, Kerala, West Bengal, Jharkhand, Gujarat and Maharashtra.
note: REPLACES L5 'By one American government count, India holds the third biggest store of it on Earth' = WRONG/OUT OF DATE. USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries 2026 (Feb 2026, rev. v1.3 May 2026) lists India's rare earth reserves as NA, footnote 14: 'A 2015 report from OSCOM indicated that monazite reserves from their operations were 256,000 tons; rare-earth reserves were not reported.' Only MCS 2025 (Jan 2025) showed India 3rd at 6,900,000 t (after China 44 Mt, Brazil 21 Mt; Brazil since revised to 11 Mt). DAE still cites the 2025 edition (PIB 12 Mar 2026: 'world’s third largest rare earth resources'); IBM Yearbook 2022 says 'fifth largest'; Reuters (Jun 2025) said 'fifth-largest'. Do not state a rank. Figure is AMD in-situ resource, not mineable reserve: on-screen '7.23 MILLION TONNES · DAE/AMD 2026'.

claim: A rare earth magnet is mostly iron, about 1% boron and roughly 30% rare earth metal such as neodymium
source_quote: Sintered NdFeB magnets are composed of roughly 30% RE material, 69% iron, and 1% boron by weight.
note: US DOE Rare Earth Permanent Magnets supply chain deep dive, 24 Feb 2022 (primary). RE material = Nd plus Pr, Dy. On-screen if used: ~69% IRON · ~1% BORON · ~30% RARE EARTHS.

claim: These magnets are small but very strong (strongest magnets commercially available)
source_quote: Sintered NdFeB magnets are the strongest magnets commercially available
note: PIB backgrounder 2 Feb 2026: REPMs 'are among the strongest types of permanent magnets'.

claim: A stronger magnet lets a smaller, lighter motor give the same push, so the vehicle goes further on a charge
source_quote: The higher maximum energy product of NdFeB at temperatures up to about 180 degrees Celsius allows manufacturers to reduce the size and weight of components (or achieve higher efficiency out of components of the same size).
note: DOE also: rare earth magnets enable 'more efficient, more powerful, and lighter-weight motors in electric vehicles (EVs)'. USGS FS 087-02: 'Use of REE magnets reduces the weight of automobiles.' The km gain is a qualitative principle: any number on the HUD must be labelled ILLUSTRATIVE.

claim: Most electric cars use these magnets in their traction motors
source_quote: It is estimated that between 90% and 100% of battery and hybrid electric vehicles will have synchronous traction motors with NdFeB magnets by 2025.
note: DOE 2022 (primary).

claim: Most electric scooters on Indian roads use rare earth magnets in their motors
source_quote: These companies currently use medium and heavy rare earth magnets, which they used to import from China, on their vehicles.
note: Business Standard 12 Jun 2025 (leading e2W makers). ET via Outlook Business (Jul 2025): Bajaj, Ather, TVS and Ola 'account for eight out of every ten EV-two-wheelers sold' and all depended on these magnets (Ola had stockpiled them). Ola certified a ferrite (rare-earth-free) motor in Oct 2025, so 'most' not 'all'.

claim: The same kind of magnet sits in a phone's small vibration motor
source_quote: iPhone SE (3rd generation) is made with 100 percent recycled rare earth elements in the Taptic Engine and audio magnets.
note: Apple Product Environmental Report, Mar 2022 (primary). The Taptic Engine is the iPhone's haptic (vibration) motor. DOE 2022 also lists 'cell phones' among NdFeB uses.

claim: These magnets are also used in many wind turbines and in defence systems
source_quote: Rare earth magnets have many uses across a broad spectrum of applications, including wind turbines, electric vehicle drives, hard disk drives, cell phones, loudspeakers, industrial motors, non-drivetrain motors in vehicles, power tools, and electric bikes.
note: DOE also: 'including clean energy and defense technologies'. PIB 2 Feb 2026: used in 'wind turbine generators ... defence equipment'. DOE says not all wind turbines use them (the common geared DFIG design has none), hence 'many wind turbines' in the live vo.txt.

claim: India needs about four thousand tonnes of rare earth magnets a year (replacement for L14)
source_quote: the country’s current requirement of rare earth permanent magnets is about 4,000 tonnes, which is projected to rise to nearly 8,000 tonnes by 2030
note: PIB (DAE), Dr Jitendra Singh in Lok Sabha, 25 Mar 2026. REPLACES L14 'India brought in about fifty-three thousand tonnes of permanent magnets' = WRONG in context (viewer hears 53,000 t of these rare earth magnets). The 53,748 t (FY2024-25, Reuters 26 Nov 2025) is the customs total for 'permanent magnets of metal' (HS 8505.11), mostly cheap non-rare-earth magnets: UN Comtrade (India, CY2024, HS 850511) = 54,452 t worth US$198.6 million, i.e. about US$3.6 per kg (our calculation), a ferrite-level price; China exported only 58,152 t of rare earth magnets to the whole world in 2024 (Adamas Intelligence, from China customs data); the government puts India's rare earth magnet need at about 4,000 t a year.

claim: Almost all rare earth magnets used in India are imported (replacement for L14)
source_quote: At present, India’s demand for REPMs is met primarily through imports.
note: PMIndia Cabinet release, 26 Nov 2025 (primary). Reuters (Kitco, 26 Nov 2025) quoting minister Ashwini Vaishnaw: 'Right now, all permanent magnets used in the country are imported from somewhere'.

claim: More than eight out of every ten of India's imported magnets come from China (replacement for L15)
source_quote: with imports mainly from China, meeting most of the demand (nearly 60–80% by value and 85–90% by quantity between 2022–25)
note: PIB backgrounder, 2 Feb 2026 (primary). ICRA (IANS, 12 Jun 2025): India imported about US$200 million of NdFeB magnets in FY2025, 'approximately 85 per cent' from China. REPLACES L15 'about nine out of every ten tonnes' (tied to the 53,748 t figure). On-screen: 85–90% FROM CHINA (BY WEIGHT, 2022–25).

claim: Rare earths are not actually rare: they are relatively abundant in the Earth's crust
source_quote: Rare earths are relatively abundant in the Earth’s crust, but minable concentrations are less common than for most other mineral commodities.
note: USGS MCS 2026 (primary). USGS FS 087-02: 'actually more abundant than many familiar industrial metals'.

claim: The hard part is getting them out clean: separating them is complex because their chemistry is so similar
source_quote: There is a significant gap in knowledge and equilibrium data for solvent extraction used for rare earth separation, which is a complex process due to the similar chemical properties of many rare earth elements found together.
note: IEA Global Critical Minerals Outlook 2026 (Jul 2026), p. 287 (primary).

claim: There are seventeen rare earth elements
source_quote: Rare Earths are a group of 17 elements starting with lanthanum in the periodic table of elements and include scandium and yttrium.
note: Indian Minerals Yearbook 2022, Rare Earths chapter (IBM, primary).

claim: When you dig rare earths up, you get them mixed together (replacement wording for L18)
source_quote: There is a significant gap in knowledge and equilibrium data for solvent extraction used for rare earth separation, which is a complex process due to the similar chemical properties of many rare earth elements found together.
note: REPLACES '...you get all of them mixed together' with '...you get them mixed together': not all 17 turn up in ore. IBM 2020: rare earths are found in the crust 'with the exception of the highly-unstable promethium'; USGS FS 087-02 counts '15 naturally occurring REE'.

claim: Rare earths are like twins: nearly the same size, almost the same chemistry, hard to tell apart
source_quote: Although the 15 naturally occurring REE (table 1; fig. 2) are generally similar in their geochemical properties, their individual abundances in the Earth are by no means equal.
note: USGS Fact Sheet 087-02 (primary). Twins analogy is narration; live vo.txt says 'Nearly the same size' (USGS: 'generally similar', not identical).

claim: Separation: the mix is dissolved in acid and flows through a row of tanks; each tank separates neighbouring rare earths only a little
source_quote: Most of the adjacent rare earths have separation factors which are near one, which means that a large number of stages are needed to produce a good separation.
note: AIME/SME paper 1972 (abstract). IEA GCMO 2026: China 'predominantly uses chloride routes (hydrochloric acid) that require polyvinyl chloride (PVC) tanks and cells'.

claim: A big plant can run hundreds of these tanks in a row to get one element clean
source_quote: The counter-current flow multistage mixer-settler of FIG. 1 included an extracting section A of 72 stages, a scrubbing section B of 72 stages, and a back-extracting section C of 8 stages.
note: Patent example: 152 mixer-settler stages to take one Nd/Pr mix to 99.9% neodymium. EU H2020 NEMO project slide (2022): 'Conventional process: 1000s of stages comprising numerous extraction-scrubbing-stripping cycles'. Any tank count drawn on screen: label ILLUSTRATIVE.

claim: The clean rare earth is made into metal, melted with iron and boron, and cooled into thin pieces (strip casting)
source_quote: Magnet alloys can be produced by induction melting the metals, followed by strip casting, where molten metals are poured on the outer surface of a cooled metal cylinder while the cylinder is rotated to produce a directionally solidified microstructure of the alloy with a small grains size.
note: DOE 2022 (primary). IEA GCMO 2026 lists metallisation ('Refining the oxides to produce rare earth metals') and strip casting with iron as separate steps.

claim: Hydrogen gas cracks the pieces, which are then milled into powder
source_quote: This may be followed by hydrogen decrepitation to reduce the grain size further, producing a strip that is then jet milled using autogenous milling of the alloy into a powder with small grains that can be used for magnet production.
note: DOE 2022 (primary).

claim: The magnet powder is much smaller than flour (replacement wording for L26)
source_quote: The particle size used in magnet production is less than 10 microns.
note: ASABE Transactions 2014: 'The mean particle size as measured by laser diffraction was 45.6 μm and 44.5 μm for HRW and SW flour, respectively.' So the powder is under a quarter of flour's mean size (our comparison). REPLACES 'much smaller than flour dust' with 'much smaller than flour': flour is sourced, 'flour dust' (its finest part) is not sized in any source we found.

claim: The powder is lined up in a strong magnetic field, pressed into a block and baked at about a thousand degrees
source_quote: The powder is then aligned and pressed in a magnetic field, followed by sintering at 1,000-1,100°C.
note: DOE 2022 (primary). On-screen: ~1,000–1,100 °C.

claim: Only at the end is the block charged into a magnet (magnetised)
source_quote: After plating, the magnet is magnetized in a high magnetic field to align the magnetization of the grains in the magnet.
note: DOE 2022 (primary).

claim: The chain runs: mixed rare earths to clean rare earth powder (oxide) to metal to alloy to magnet
source_quote: The Scheme will support the creation of integrated REPM manufacturing facilities, involving conversion of rare earth oxides to metals, metals to alloys, and alloys to finished REPMs.
note: PMIndia 26 Nov 2025 (primary). IEA GCMO 2026 shows the same stages: mining, separation, metallisation, alloy production, magnet production.

claim: China leads every link of the chain, with the biggest share of each (replacement wording for L31)
source_quote: In 2024, the People’s Republic of China (hereafter, “China”) accounted for 60% of global mined production of magnet rare earths. For refining, the level of concentration is more pronounced, as the country represented 91% of global refined output.
note: REPLACES 'end up holding almost every link' with 'end up leading every link': China has the biggest share of each link, but mining is about 60%, not 'almost' all. IEA Rare Earth Elements report, executive summary (Apr 2026).

claim: In 1992 Deng Xiaoping is reported to have said: the Middle East has oil, China has rare earths
source_quote: “The Middle East has oil,” Deng Xiaoping is reported to have remarked. “China has rare earths.” Deng was visiting one of China’s biggest rare earths mines, in Baotou, Inner Mongolia, in 1992 when he made that observation
note: Year disputed: CSIS (2019) says 'Former Chinese leader Deng Xiaoping famously said in 1987 that while “the Middle East has oil, China has rare earths,”'. No transcript or official record of the remark was found. 1992 is the most cited date (Asia Times 2026: a visit to Baotou; Chinese media tie it to his 1992 southern tour). VO already says 'is reported to have said' - keep. On-screen tag: REPORTED. Other date (1987) goes in the description/pinned note.

claim: China treated rare earths as a national, state-backed mission
source_quote: This drastic shift was not a coincidence but rather the consequence of a concerted effort by the Chinese government to “strategically” flood the global rare-earth market, according to the U.S. Department of Defense.
note: CSIS 2019 (citing US DoD). 'Like a family business' is narration analogy.

claim: Until about forty years ago (mid-1980s) America made most of the world's rare earths
source_quote: From 1965 through the mid-1980s, Mountain Pass was the dominant source of REE, and the United States was largely self-sufficient in REE.
note: USGS FS 087-02: 'the Mountain Pass era, starting in 1965 and ending about 1984'. CSIS 2019: 'From the 1960s to the 1980s, the United States was the world’s leading producer of rare-earth elements'. The Conversation (2026): Mountain Pass 'led world production of rare earths until the late 1980s'. 2026 minus 1984-1989 = 37-42 years, fits 'about forty'.

claim: The work moved to China, where labour was cheaper and pollution rules were weaker
source_quote: State support coupled with lower labor costs and less stringent environmental standards enabled China’s rare-earth rise.
note: Asia Times (Jan 2026): 'the Americans gradually shifted the production to China, enticed by lower environmental standards and lower labor costs.'

claim: Separating rare earths is dirty work (strong acids, lots of waste) and other countries were happy to let someone else do it
source_quote: Buyers using processing in China got material below the cost of making it themselves, and none of the cleanup bills or the bad press.
note: Same article: 'separation produces acidic, and sometimes radioactive, residues' and radioactive wastewater spills at Mountain Pass. IEA GCMO 2026: 'Methods that avoid highly contaminating strong acids' listed as a bottleneck.

claim: China has done this work for about thirty-plus years (head start of more than thirty years)
source_quote: Four periods of production are evident: the monazite-placer era, starting in the late 1800s and ending abruptly in 1964; the Mountain Pass era, starting in 1965 and ending about 1984; a transitional period from about 1984 to 1991; and the Chinese era, beginning about 1991.
note: Chinese era from about 1991 = about 35 years to 2026 (our calculation).

claim: IEA: China mines about sixty percent of the rare earths used in magnets
source_quote: its share in mined supply of magnet rare earths declining from around 60% in 2025 to 55% in 2035 in the base case
note: IEA GCMO 2026, Jul 2026 (2025 data). IEA Rare Earth Elements report (Apr 2026): 60% in 2024. Magnet rare earths = Nd, Pr, Dy, Tb. On-screen: IEA · MINED ~60% (2025).

claim: IEA: China separates/refines about eighty-five percent of magnet rare earths (replacement for L38)
source_quote: For refining, China’s share dropped from 90% to 85% between 2024 and 2025, with the majority of the lost share being claimed by the United States and the rest by Malaysia
note: REPLACES 'It separates about nine in every ten' (91% was the 2024 figure in the IEA Rare Earth Elements report, Apr 2026; the newer IEA Global Critical Minerals Outlook 2026, July 2026, gives 85% for 2025; annex: China 75 of 89 kt refined). On-screen: REFINED ~85% (2025).

claim: IEA: China makes about ninety-four percent of the world's sintered rare earth magnets (replacement wording for L38)
source_quote: In 2005, China accounted for around 50% of the production of sintered permanent magnets, but its share expanded significantly to reach 94% in 2024.
note: REPLACES 'the world's strongest magnets' with 'these strong magnets': IEA's 94% is for sintered permanent magnets (2024 data, IEA Rare Earth Elements report, Apr 2026; no newer IEA figure found). DOE calls sintered NdFeB 'the strongest magnets commercially available', so the old wording was not false, but it can be heard as all magnets. On-screen: SINTERED MAGNETS 94% (2024).

claim: Digging is the easy part; separation, metal and magnet making are the hard part, and China runs most of it (replacement wording for L39)
source_quote: However, significant technology gaps remain in the separation, metallisation and magnet production stages.
note: IEA GCMO 2026 also: 'Mining technologies and equipment are generally less of a bottleneck'. REPLACES '...and China owns them' with '...and China runs most of them' (85% refining, 94% magnets, not all).

claim: In India rare earths come mainly from monazite, found in beach sands on the south and east coasts
source_quote: In India, monazite is the principal source of rare earths and thorium.
note: World Nuclear Association (Oct 2026): '12 Mt of which are in heavy mineral sands deposits on the south and east coasts of India.'

claim: Monazite carries thorium, a radioactive element that can be used as nuclear fuel
source_quote: Thorium fuels can breed fissile uranium-233 to be used in various kinds of nuclear reactors.
note: PIB 23 Jul 2025: monazite is 'a mineral of Thorium (~10% ThO2) and Rare Earths (~55% REO)'. IBM 2020: monazite 'is radio active in nature'. WNA: thorium is fertile, used with a fissile driver.

claim: By law monazite is an atomic (prescribed) substance under the Atomic Energy Act
source_quote: The mineral monazite is a prescribed substance as per the Notification under the Atomic Energy Act, 1962.
note: IBM Indian Minerals Yearbook 2022 (primary). PIB 29 Jan 2026: 'the prescribed substance monazite'.

claim: Only one government company, IREL, is allowed to process monazite
source_quote: IREL is the only entity processing monazite to produce Rare-earth (RE) compounds.
note: PIB (DAE, Apr 2025): IREL 'has been mandated to produce Rare Earth Elements ... from ... Monazite in India'. Outlook Business (2025): 'India restricted rare earth mining under the Atomic Energy Act, allowing only IREL'. No 2025-26 change found that lets private firms process monazite (2023 MMDR change covers other rare earth minerals).

claim: Indian Rare Earths Limited is now called IREL (India) Limited
source_quote: IREL (India) Limited (IREL), a PSU under Department of Atomic Energy produces Rare Earth Elements in the form of high pure rare earth oxides from RE bearing mineral Monazite in India.
note: Old name: PIB 9 Oct 2015 'Indian Rare Earths Limited (IREL) has set up facilities for producing separated high pure RE oxides'. Say 'I.R.E.L.' in VO (lint rule).

claim: For decades the state-only set-up kept India's rare earth business small
source_quote: The source of India’s production gap is regulatory.
note: ORF analysis (2026). DAE (PIB 12 Mar 2026): 'despite adequate rare-earth resources, the production capacities are at a limited level on account of absence of mid-stream and downstream industries in the RE value chain.' Narration presents it as reasoning ('If you think about it').

claim: India's own mining bureau (IBM) wrote that domestic demand for rare earths was limited
source_quote: Domestic demand for the rare-earths is limited at present and is mainly catered to by IREL for rare earth elements available in Indian deposits (5 Nos.) and by resorting to import for rare-earth elements (rest of 17) not available in Indian resources.
note: Indian Minerals Yearbook 2020, Rare Earths chapter (published 2022). Document push-in OK; quote the line exactly.

claim: In 2024 IREL produced about 2,900 tonnes of rare earths
source_quote: In 2024, Toyotsu shipped more than 1,000t of rare earth materials to Japan, a significant portion of the 2,900t mined by IREL.
note: Mining Technology citing Reuters (Jun 2025). USGS MCS 2026: India 2024 mine production 2,900 t REO (estimate). Outlook Business: Japan exports were 'about a third of IREL’s total output'.

claim: More than 1,000 tonnes went to Japan in 2024 under a deal signed in 2012
source_quote: Under the 2012 agreement, IREL supplies rare earths to Toyotsu Rare Earths India, a subsidiary of Toyota Tsusho, for processing and subsequent export to Japan.
note: Same article: 'In 2024, Toyotsu shipped more than 1,000t of rare earth materials to Japan'. Outlook Business: '13-year-old export agreement with Toyota Tsusho’s Indian unit'.

claim: India sends rare earth material out and buys finished magnets in
source_quote: At present, India’s demand for REPMs is met primarily through imports.
note: Outbound side: R50 (Toyotsu exports to Japan). 'Cheap out, expensive in' is narration (value added in magnets).

claim: Indian monazite is rich in the lighter rare earths such as neodymium
source_quote: Further Monazite resource predominantly contains light rare earth elements while heavy rare earth elements are not available in economically extractable quantities.
note: PIB (DAE, Rajya Sabha reply, 12 Mar 2026). IBM 2022 lists neodymium among REEs 'in supply surplus' in India.

claim: A magnet in a hot motor needs a little of two heavier rare earths (dysprosium, terbium) to keep its strength in the heat
source_quote: heavy REs such as dysprosium (Dy) and terbium (Tb) are used primarily in sintered magnets to improve their resistance to demagnetization at temperatures above 120 degrees C.
note: DOE 2022 (primary). On-screen: DYSPROSIUM · TERBIUM.

claim: India's Department of Atomic Energy says India has very little of those heavy rare earths, so India depends on others for them
source_quote: Further Monazite resource predominantly contains light rare earth elements while heavy rare earth elements are not available in economically extractable quantities.
note: PIB (DAE), Rajya Sabha reply, 12 Mar 2026 - matches the live VO attribution 'Our own atomic energy department says'. IBM Yearbook 2022 agrees: 'Dysprosium, Terbium, Europium which are classified as HREE are having supply constraint. These HREEs are not available in Indian deposits in extractable quantity.' The writer had marked this contested; both official sources agree.

claim: April 2025: China made exporters get licences for seven medium and heavy rare earths and magnets made with them
source_quote: 4. Dysprosium-containing neodymium-iron-boron permanent magnetic materials.
note: MOFCOM/GACC Announcement No. 18 of 2025 (4 Apr 2025), reproduced by CIRS: items cover Sm, Gd, Tb, Dy, Lu, Sc, Y plus samarium-cobalt and Tb/Dy-containing NdFeB magnet materials. USGS MCS 2026: 'In April 2025, China tightened its export controls on rare-earth elements, adding specific controls on alloys, compounds, metals, and oxides of samarium, gadolinium, terbium, dysprosium, lutetium, scandium, and yttrium.'

claim: Licences take time, and the waits caused magnet shortages
source_quote: Approvals are taking longer, although generally still within the commerce ministry's 45 business day deadline, said the other, but the scrutiny is now similar to April, at the height of the trade war, when lengthy waits for licenses caused magnet shortages that led to shutdowns at automotive factories.
note: Reuters via Business Standard, 14 Oct 2025.

claim: By July 2025 Bajaj was making about half the Chetaks it made a year earlier
source_quote: Our component inventory saw us through until June, but we are down by half in terms of production in the current month, and I am afraid that we are looking at a zero month in August as of now.
note: Rajiv Bajaj to ET, Jul 2025. Autocar: 10,824 vs 20,384 = 53% of a year earlier (47% fall).

claim: Ather and TVS felt the magnet squeeze too (replacement for L54 second sentence)
source_quote: The disruptions in the EV supply chain, particularly concerning magnet availability, continue to pose challenges in the short to medium term. We are working actively to mitigate the prevailing challenges.
note: TVS Motor spokesperson (FE, Jul 2025). Ather: Autocar India 5 Aug 2025 'Ather is facing a short-term supply challenge as a rare earth magnet shortage from China disrupts dealer inventory supply.' REPLACES 'Ather and T.V.S. cut production too': ET (4 Jul 2025, unnamed sources) only said they were set to cut; Autocar's July 2025 data show TVS iQube output up 6% (23,742) and Ather up 45% (16,148) year on year, and Ather's CEO said it was 'not a full halt in production, but a supply gap'.

claim: Back in April 2025 Rajiv Bajaj warned that if China stopped these magnets, India's EV industry could halt within weeks (replacement for L55)
source_quote: Speaking to Moneycontrol, Bajaj said, “If this is true, it would mean that in a matter of weeks, the entire Indian EV industry will grind to a halt.”
note: CNBC-TV18, 28 Apr 2025. Moneycontrol video transcript: 'if it doesn't change, then in a matter of weeks, the entire Indian EV industry will grind to a halt'. REPLACES L55 timing: the old line sits after 'By July' and reads as if he spoke after July; he spoke in late April and his warning was conditional. Present as his warning (claim).

claim: Later China gave licences to some Indian firms, on condition the magnets were not used for defence
source_quote: The import licenses have specific conditions attached. The imported magnets cannot be re-exported to the United States and cannot be used for defence-related purposes.
note: IANS 30 Oct 2025 (MEA confirmed licences). Drishti IAS 31 Oct 2025: licences limit 'use to non-defence applications such as vehicle components'.

claim: October 2025: China announced wider rules; after talks with America it put them on hold for one year
source_quote: In October, China expanded its rare-earths export controls to include europium, holmium, erbium, thulium, and ytterbium. In November, China suspended the October export controls for 1 year.
note: MOFCOM Announcement No. 70 (7 Nov 2025) suspended Nos. 55-58, 61, 62. The Conversation (2026): 'After President Donald Trump met Chinese leader Xi Jinping that month, Beijing suspended six export controls until Nov. 10, 2026'.

claim: On paper, the hold ends on 10 November 2026 (replacement for L58)
source_quote: 经批准，自即日起至2026年11月10日，商务部、海关总署公告2025年第55号、56号、57号、58号，及商务部公告2025年第61号、62号暂停实施。
note: MOFCOM/GACC Announcement No. 70 of 2025 (7 Nov 2025): 'With approval, from today until 10 November 2026, Announcements 55, 56, 57, 58, 61 and 62 are suspended.' (our translation).

claim: In September 2026 America and China agreed to stretch their truce to 10 January 2027 (replacement for L58)
source_quote: 本次经贸磋商中，中美双方同意在将吉隆坡经贸磋商联合安排延期至2027年1月10日的基础上，继续积极探讨这一事项，旨在达成双方同意的解决方案。
note: MOFCOM, 28 Sep 2026: the two sides agreed, on the basis of extending the Kuala Lumpur joint arrangement (which paused measures until 10 Nov 2026) to 10 Jan 2027, to keep discussing (our translation). Steptoe 28 Sep 2026: Bessent said the truce 'will be extended to January 10, 2027'.

claim: It is not yet clear whether China's hold moves to January along with the truce; no new legal notice had been published as of mid-October 2026 (replacement for L58)
source_quote: China’s one-year pause on its October 2025 rare-earth export controls runs until 10 November 2026 under Announcement No. 70, and no notice extending it appeared on the commerce ministry’s 2026 list as of 16 October.
note: Disputed reading: BISI (late Sep 2026) and Brownstein say the suspension itself now runs to 10 Jan 2027; Startup Fortune (20 Oct 2026, citing Bloomberg Government) and rare-earth-mining.com (11 Oct) say the truce statement never named the rare earth suspension. Old L58 ('runs out on November tenth, twenty twenty-six, unless China extends it') ignores the 28 Sep truce extension; new L58 says the legal date, the truce extension, and that the viewer should watch whether the hold goes with it. Description/pinned note: 'China's legal notice still says 10 Nov 2026; the US-China truce now runs to 10 Jan 2027 (as of 21 Oct 2026).' RE-CHECK RIGHT BEFORE UPLOAD.

claim: China's April 2025 licence rule never went away
source_quote: The April export controls remained in effect, although China began to issue general export licenses to selected exporters.
note: USGS MCS 2026 (primary). technology.org 19 Oct 2026: the pause 'never covered China’s April 2025 licensing regime'.

claim: India runs a rare earth magnet plant in Visakhapatnam on a Bhabha Atomic Research Centre campus
source_quote: The facility for production of Rare Earth Permanent Magnet has been developed in the campus of Bhabha Atomic Research Centre at Visakhapatnam.
note: PIB (PMO), 10 May 2023: dedicated to the nation on 11 May 2023. PIB (DAE) 29 Jan 2026: 'a Rare Earth Permanent Magnet plant has been operationalized at Vizag for production of Samarium Cobalt magnets.'

claim: The plant is built on Indian technology from BARC and a DRDO lab (DMRL)
source_quote: Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC) has developed a novel metallurgical process for making RE alloy powder using indigenous RE oxides prepared by IREL. The technology for converting the RE alloys to magnets is available with Defence Metallurgical Research Laboratory, Hyderabad.
note: PIB (DAE) 9 Oct 2015; PIB 10 May 2023: 'established based on indigenous technology'. Say 'D.R.D.O.' in VO.

claim: It makes samarium-cobalt magnets that stay stable at high temperatures, used in defence and space
source_quote: Rare Earth (RE) magnets, such as samarium-cobalt, find use in Atomic Energy, Space and Defence industries for a variety of strategic and non-strategic applications. These exhibit superior quality in terms of performance ability, device miniaturization capability and stability at high operating temperatures.
note: PIB (Earth Sciences) 2 Apr 2026: Vizag plant makes '3 tons Samarium Cobalt (SmCo) magnets annually which are high-performance rare-earth magnets commonly used in strategic sectors such as defence and atomic energy'. DOE 2022: SmCo 'more resistant to demagnetization at higher temperatures than NdFeB'. Note: PIB 25 Mar 2026 gives '500 tonnes per year' initial capacity, which conflicts with 3 t; the VO gives no capacity, so keep it that way.

claim: In November 2025 the government approved a 7,280 crore rupee magnet scheme
source_quote: The Union Cabinet chaired by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today approved the ‘Scheme to Promote Manufacturing of Sintered Rare Earth Permanent Magnets’ with a financial outlay of Rs.7280 crore.
note: PMIndia, 26 Nov 2025 (primary). Reuters (Kitco) same day.

claim: The scheme's goal is 6,000 tonnes of magnets a year made in India
source_quote: This first-of-its-kind initiative aims to establish 6,000 Metric Tons per Annum (MTPA) of integrated Rare Earth Permanent Magnet (REPM) manufacturing in India
note: Full chain oxide to metal to alloy to magnet: see R30.

claim: Five companies can win up to 1,200 tonnes a year each
source_quote: The scheme envisions allocating the total capacity to five beneficiaries through a global competitive bidding process. Each beneficiary will be allotted up to 1,200 MTPA of capacity.
note: DD India 13 Aug 2026 repeats it.

claim: In August 2026, twenty bids came in, with Larsen and Toubro, Coal India and ReNew among the bidders
source_quote: The bidders include 20 Microns Limited, Attero Recycling Private Limited, Coal India Limited, Larsen & Toubro Limited, Lohum Magnets & Energy Solutions Private Limited, NEO Performance Materials (Singapore) PTE. LTD., Proterial (India) Limited, Prozeal Green Energy Limited, Renew Private Limited and Shankaranarayana Constructions Limited, among others.
note: DD India 13 Aug 2026 (MHI received 20 bids; technical bids opened 13 Aug). PSU Watch 14 Aug 2026: 'Three of the 20 entries are joint bids.' So say 'twenty bids came in', not 'twenty companies put in bids' (small VO fix).

claim: The winners had not been announced as of 21 October 2026
source_quote: Selection of Manufacturers for Establishing Integrated Sintered NdFeB Rare Earth Permanent Magnet Manufacturing Facilities under the Scheme to Promote Manufacturing of Sintered Rare Earth Permanent Magnet - Addendum-3 29-07-2026
note: Ministry of Heavy Industries scheme page checked 21 Oct 2026: the latest document is Addendum-3 of 29 Jul 2026; no award notice. News searches found no award. RE-CHECK RIGHT BEFORE UPLOAD.

claim: The 2026-27 Union Budget announced special rare earth zones (officially Rare Earth Corridors) in Odisha, Kerala, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu for mining, processing, research and manufacturing
source_quote: Union Budget 2026–27 announces Dedicated Rare Earth Corridors in Odisha, Kerala, Andhra Pradesh, and Tamil Nadu for mining, processing, research, and manufacturing of Rare Earth Permanent Magnets (REPMs).
note: PIB backgrounder 2 Feb 2026; PIB 2 Apr 2026 repeats it. Official name is 'Rare Earth Corridors': VO 'zones' is a fair paraphrase; on-screen label should read RARE EARTH CORRIDORS (optional VO 'special rare earth corridors').

claim: In June 2025 Reuters reported India asked IREL to stop rare earth exports to Japan and keep them at home
source_quote: India has reportedly requested state-owned miner IREL to suspend rare earth exports to Japan, a move that could affect a 13-year-old supply agreement, reported Reuters, citing sources.
note: Reuters 16-17 Jun 2025 (TrendForce 17 Jun 2025; AutocarPro). VO attributes it to Reuters - keep. Same report: 'an immediate halt to exports to Japan may not be feasible'. No later report confirms exports actually stopped (see R83).

claim: The plan now is to keep India's rare earths at home (replacement for L69 first sentence)
source_quote: With China’s recent export restrictions causing global supply chain concerns, IREL is looking to retain its rare earths for domestic expansion in mining and processing.
note: REPLACES 'So the sand stays here.' (states as done what was only reported as a request; no confirmation found that IREL's Japan exports stopped).

claim: Under the scheme, plants get two years to be built, then five years of support
source_quote: The total duration of the scheme will be 7 years from the date of award, including a 2-year gestation period for setting up an integrated REPM manufacturing facility, and 5 years for incentive disbursement on the sale of REPM.
note: PMIndia 26 Nov 2025 (primary).

claim: Running separation and magnet plants well takes practice; it cannot be bought overnight
source_quote: These are areas that require training, practice and time to hone techniques and build a skilled workforce.
note: IEA GCMO 2026, p. 288 (about separation data, sintering protocols and magnet cutting).

claim: India already separates rare earths to oxide, but has no industrial-scale alloy or magnet plants (replacement wording for L74)
source_quote: While India has existing facilities from mining to separation and refining to oxide form and also developed capability of metal extraction, further industrial scale facilities (intermediate) from alloy, magnet etc. is non-existent.
note: REPLACES 'What's left is the hard middle — the tanks and the furnaces.' with '... — more tanks, and the furnaces.' I.R.E.L. already runs separation tanks; the gap is scale plus alloy and magnet furnaces. 'It has the scientists' = BARC/DMRL (R67); 'the money' = the scheme (R69).

claim: Magnet supply can affect whether a scooter reaches the showroom on time
source_quote: For buyers, this slowdown could mean longer waiting periods for the Chetak in the coming months.
note: Phones contain these magnets: R13. 'Its price' is framed as a dependency, not a measured price rise; Rajiv Bajaj (ET Jul 2025) also flagged cost increases.

claim: India is called the pharmacy of the world
source_quote: India’s standing as the Pharmacy of the World is rooted in the unique combination of affordable pricing and assured quality, which has made Indian medicines widely preferred across global markets.
note: PIB backgrounder, 21 Mar 2026.

claim: A big share of the ingredients in Indian medicines comes from China
source_quote: Import from China was almost 71.72 per cent of the overall bulk drug imports during the fiscal year.
note: Pharmabiz (May 2024) from DGCI&S/DoP data, FY2023-24 (76% by quantity). PIB (Cabinet, 21 Mar 2020): 'India is significantly dependent on import of basic raw materials, viz., Bulk Drugs that are used to produce medicines. In some specific bulk drugs the import dependence is 80 to 100%.' PIB (DoP, 10 Mar 2026) lists APIs where China is 70-100% of imports (e.g. rifampicin, methyldopa at 100%). If a number is shown: 'ABOUT 7 IN 10 IMPORTED BULK DRUGS FROM CHINA (FY24)'.

claim: No later confirmation that IREL's exports to Japan actually stopped (context for L68-L69)
source_quote: However, India may not be able to halt supplies to Japan immediately, as they are governed by a bilateral agreement between the two governments, Reuters reports, citing sources.
note: TrendForce 17 Jun 2025 relaying Reuters. Searches through 21 Oct 2026 found no IREL/DAE statement or later report that the Japan exports stopped or resumed. This row backs the softer L69 wording.
